newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia faces problems if reforms not implemented.
newsitem.headline: Russia faces problems if reforms not implemented.

text.p: Russia has not yet emerged from an economic crisis and its financial system will be under a heavy strain if reforms are not implemented this year, Finance Minister Alexander Livshits said on Tuesday.
"We have not emerged from the crisis yet," Livshits told a news conference.
He said Russia had not yet adjusted to low inflation rates, while the government was preparing to introduce major reforms of taxation and of military and social spending.
"If we do not implement them this year it will be very difficult for the financial system to function," Livshits said.
The new Tax Code will go to the cabinet at the end of February and then to the State Duma lower house of parliament, he said.
Livshits said he expected the biggest battle to be fought over preserving tax privileges, which this year amount to 160 trillion roubles.
"The main idea of the new Code is to liquidate privileges, otherwise we shall have to increase the fiscal pressure, which no one likes," Livshits said.

On Monday first deputy Duma speaker Alexander Shokhin, a former economy minister and chief debt negotiator, warned Russia could default if it did not implement financial reforms properly, and Livshits backed this view when asked to comment.
"If we do not implement reforms in 1997, the forecast of a default could be justified," he said.
